chosen.title: The Robot Beside You: What Humanoid Machines Actually Do on the Factory Floor in 2026
chosen.rationale: Figure 02 at BMW's Spartanburg plant, Digit inside Amazon fulfillment centers, Atlas at Hyundai's Georgia facility, and Apollo on Mercedes-Benz assembly lines mark 2026 as the year humanoid robots crossed from demo to deployment — and the real story is the gap between Hollywood's vision and the precise, narrow material-handling jobs these machines actually perform. Kenji's 'explain the mechanism' mandate fits perfectly: why bipedal form matters in human-designed spaces, what ±2mm repeatability means versus ±0.02mm for fixed arms, how AI perception/navigation enables the flexibility trade-off, and what it looks like for a human worker to take a shift alongside a robot colleague.

rejected_candidates.title: The AI Lab Partner: How Scientific AI Is Compressing Decades of Discovery Into Months
rejected_candidates.rationale: Anthropic launched Claude Science on June 30 as its newest flagship product — two days ago — positioning AI as an autonomous research collaborator that can identify drug candidates, run code on compute clusters, and perform at 'second-year grad student' level in physics and computational biology. MIT and Recursion simultaneously released Boltz-2, delivering 1,000× faster binding affinity predictions than conventional methods. This is a decisive inflection: AI moving from paper-summarizer to hypothesis-generator running real experiments. Kenji's deep-dive lens — explaining how these systems actually reason about molecular structures, generate and test hypotheses, and feed back into the scientific method — is exactly the story no one is telling for a general audience.

rejected_candidates.title: The Untethered Model: How On-Device AI Is Bringing Intelligence to the Places the Cloud Never Reached
rejected_candidates.rationale: By mid-2026, 80% of AI inference is happening locally on devices — not in data centers — as Qualcomm, Apple, and MediaTek NPUs now run production LLMs at sub-20ms latency on $400 phones. The shift is driven by quantization, model compression, and hardware co-design, but the human story is even bigger: on-device AI means private conversations that never leave your phone, real-time translation in rural clinics without internet, and AI tools that work in the 3 billion people-sized gap the cloud infrastructure never served. A perfect Kenji mechanism piece: explain how a 7B-parameter model fits on a phone chip, what precision trade-offs make it possible, and what becomes real for ordinary people when the cloud dependency disappears.
